thread:
maria: Heads-up — acme-inc reports that their service endpoint api.acme.internal suddenly returns NXDOMAIN after we cut over their VPC peering this morning. They can hit public API hostname fine, but the service endpoint inside VPC is dead. Repro steps from their pod below.

acme-sre: repro steps they ran from a pod in VPC-A:
```
# from pod
$ dig +short api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
# no output
$ dig api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +noall +answer
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +noall +answer
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```
They also tried curl to the service endpoint IP but dns lookup fails.

eli.sre: Thanks — can you paste the VPC ID and the service endpoint ARN? Also, did this start immediately after peering?

acme-sre: VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d; endpoint: com.amazonaws.vpce.svc-abcdef1234567890.us-west-2.vpce. Yes started right after peering was established to central-network VPC. No changes to Route53 we were told.

jonathan.eng: Quick checklist I'll throw out: 1) confirm private hosted zone for acme.internal exists and is associated to correct VPC(s); 2) check for a public hosted zone with same name shadowing lookups; 3) verify resolver rules/forwarders and priorities; 4) node-local-dns/ndots behavior.

dns-sheriff: Ran initial checks from our side — looks like there are TWO hosted zones for acme.internal: a public hosted zone (ZPUB-XXXX) and a private hosted zone (ZPRIV-YYYY). Private zone is associated only to central-network VPC, not the customer's VPC (vpc-0a1b2c3d). Because of the peering, resolver traffic is going to the central VPC resolver which prefers the public zone. That explains NXDOMAIN for the currently-associated private entries.

maria: So root cause = private hosted zone not associated to customer's VPC after peering change, plus split-hosted-zone behavior. What's the recommended remediation path? Can we add association or should we create a resolver rule in customer VPC to forward to central resolver?

eli.sre: Short term: associate private hosted zone ZPRIV-YYYY with vpc-0a1b2c3d. Command:
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZPRIV-YYYY --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d
```
That will make records resolve from within the customer's VPC. Long term: review why the association was removed/not present — automation/terraform drift when peering was created?

acme-sre: We can't change infra on their account without approval. Is there a non-invasive forwarder fix?

jonathan.eng: Alternative: add an outbound resolver rule in the customer's VPC to forward queries for acme.internal to the Route53 Resolver inbound IPs in central-network (or to the VPC resolver IP 10.0.0.2 they used). Example rule snippet:
```
aws route53resolver create-resolver-rule --creator-request-id fix-acme --name "forward-acme" --rule-type FORWARD --domain-name "acme.internal" --target-ips Ip=10.0.0.2
aws route53resolver associate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rslvr-xxxx --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d
```
This doesn't require hosted zone assoc but requires resolver rules rights.

dns-sheriff: Also check node-local-dns on EKS nodes — caches can return stale NXDOMAIN. After you fix association or rule, `kubectl exec` into a pod and `resolvectl flush-caches` (or restart node-local-dns DaemonSet) to avoid stale client cache causing false positives.

maria: For the support ticket: ask customer for permission to create resolver rule in their account OR have them request their infra team to associate the hosted zone. Provide both options. Also ask them to run these checks and paste `ip route` and `grep -i nameserver /etc/resolv.conf` from a pod.

acme-sre: They gave permission to create a resolver rule in their account (they're hands-off with AWS infra). I'll open a cross-account ops runbook.

deploy-bot: [auto] Support ticket #INC-2026-830 created and assigned to dns-sheriff.

eli.sre: I'll prepare the resolver rule commands and a small playbook for them. Also include rollback: remove rule or disassociate hosted zone if it conflicts.

maria: Thanks team. I'll send the suggested remediation options to customer and update ticket. :thumbsup:
